The gown is expected to sell for $150,000 to $300,000, but the price could go even higher. In 2023, a black-and-blue evening dress Diana wore to a 1985 dinner sold for a record $1.15 million, 11 times the pre-auction estimate.

Before its live auction, the revenge dress will be exhibited in London, Hong Kong, Geneva and New York. A portion of the proceeds from the sale will be donated to the NHS Lothian Charity on behalf of the Royal Edinburgh Hospital.

Sarah Kuta
| Daily Correspondent

September 14, 2026 11:58 a.m.

On June 29, 1994—the same day her then-estranged husband publicly acknowledged his infidelity—Diana, Princess of Wales, stepped out wearing a chic, black frock and made a fashion statement that reverberated around the world.

“Yes, absolutely,” Charles said.

“And you were?” asked Dimbleby.

“Yes,” Charles said, adding after a short pause, “until it became irretrievably broken down, us both having tried.”

The admission—which had been leaked several days earlier—sent shock waves through the royal family and deepened the couple’s marital crisis. A few hours after the documentary aired, Diana attended a party at the Serpentine Gallery, in London. She had reportedly planned to wear a different gown but opted instead for the little black dress.

Featuring an asymmetrical hemline, a pleated bodice, a side train and an off-the-shoulder neckline, the dress had been created by the Greek fashion designer Christina Stambolian for Diana three years earlier.
